subject: Subprocessor delegation for MultiTenant Connect — roster + DocuSign checklist
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@multitenant.com>
To: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Cc: Sara Patel <sara.patel@multitenant.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Oct 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Subprocessor roster + short ask before signature

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the DPA. Legal had a couple of last-minute gating items before we can route the DocuSign envelope: they need the current subprocessor roster (names + country of processing + purpose), and any known temporary or delegated subprocessor exceptions for multi-tenant deployments. We also need to confirm whether any telemetry/observability partners will store logs outside the US for our tenant routing.

Can you send the roster and flag any processors that: 1) do cross-border transfers outside the US, or 2) are considered temporary/contractor agents for <30 days? If possible, put a one-line mitigation note for each flagged entry (eg. encryption-in-transit, onshore fallbacks).

We'd like to close this by COB tomorrow in order to get procurement to countersign. If you prefer, deliver a DocuSign-ready addendum (we can e-sign) and we'll attach it to the main DPA.

Appreciate it,
Liam

--
Liam O'Connor
Head of Platform Security
MultiTenant Connect
liam@multitenant.com
From: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@multitenant.com>, Sara Patel <sara.patel@multitenant.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 21 Oct 2025 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor roster + short ask before signature

Hi Liam — thanks for the note. Forwarding our current roster (attached) and a short summary beneath. cc'ing Kim in legal ops and Marissa for any procurement redlines.

Attachment: redwood_subprocessor_roster_v2.csv (CSV: provider_name, country_of_processing, role, transfer_type, notes)
Attachment: DPA_MultiTenant_Addendum_Draft.pdf (proposed one-page addendum with explicit onshore fallback clause)

Quick flags from our side (all mitigations are one-line):
- EdgeBridge (US, CDN/telemetry): Cross-border logs to EU for caching — mitigation: TLS + egress limited to pseudo-anonymized telemetry; onshore fallback available in dedicated config.
- LogStreamly (US, observability): Temporary contractor access during rollout (14 days) — mitigation: time-limited credentials, audit logs retained for 90 days.
- KeyHarbor (US, KMS/HSM): No cross-border transfers; keys region-locked — mitigation: KMS remains in US region, HSM attestation available.

We are not aware of any other processors currently storing tenant-level logs outside the US for the standard multi-tenant deployment. If you want, Marissa can run a short procurement spot-check on the CDN telemetry path.

I'll also prepare a DocuSign-ready signature page for the addendum and send the envelope link once Kim signs off on the wording.

Best,
Jordan

--
Jordan Blake
Account Exec, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Jordan / Marissa — looking at the addendum draft. Two quick legal ops asks: 1) please add a short clause that temporary processors must have MFA and no console access (we use service accounts); 2) confirm retention windows for telemetry (we currently have 90 days for tenant diagnostic logs; aggregated metrics retained 365 days). Once those are in the PDF I'll initial and we can send to Liam's DocuSign link.

Also, Jordan: please inline the three flagged entries in the CSV top rows and mark them "flagged_for_notice" — that speeds their review.

Kim
